keyVerseText: And there came an angel of the LORD, and sat under an oak which was in Ophrah, that pertained unto Joash the Abiezrite: and his son Gideon threshed wheat by the winepress, to hide it from the Midianites. Gideon: Gr. Gedeon to hide: Heb. to cause it to flee
rootMeaning: The root word אֲבִיעֶזֶר (ʼĂbîyʻezer) means "my father is help," combining the Hebrew words for 'father' and 'help.' The term אֲבִי הָעֶזְרִי (ʼĂbîy hâ-ʻEzrîy) is derived from this root with the definite article inserted, signifying "father of the Ezrite" or belonging to the family of Abiezer. This etymology enriches the common English gloss "Abiezrite" by highlighting a personal and relational dimension—one rooted in the idea of God or a paternal figure as a source of help and support.
usageInScripture: The term אֲבִי הָעֶזְרִי appears three times in Scripture, consistently referring to descendants or members of the Abiezer family, a clan linked to Manasseh, son of Joseph. Translations vary slightly between "of the Abiezrites" and "the Abiezrite," but all emphasize familial and tribal identity. This consistent use underscores the importance of lineage and tribal affiliation in the biblical narrative, particularly in the context of Judges where family heritage shapes roles and destinies.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding אֲבִי הָעֶזְרִי as "my father is help" deepens our appreciation of God's providential care and strength extended through His people. The Abiezrites, as descendants of a name that proclaims divine help, remind believers that God is the ultimate source of aid and deliverance. This word roots the identity of a people in God's faithful assistance, a truth fulfilled supremely in Christ, who embodies divine help and salvation. Recognizing this connection encourages faith in God's ongoing support amid trials, as seen in the story of Gideon.
keyVerseReflection: In Judges 6:11, the angel of the LORD visits Joash the Abiezrite, situating the narrative within the family known for 'my father is help.' This detail highlights the providential context of Gideon's calling, emphasizing that he comes from a lineage defined by divine assistance. The word אֲבִי הָעֶזְרִי enriches the verse by linking Gideon's hidden threshing work and forthcoming deliverance to a heritage of help and hope rooted in God's faithfulness.
